basics.name: Sunil Simha
basics.label: Brinson Postdoctoral Fellow
basics.summary: Observational astronomer studying Fast Radio Bursts as probes of the circumgalactic and intergalactic media. Research interests include matter density distribution in the universe, galaxy evolution and feedback, and observational cosmology.

work.name: University of Chicago & Northwestern University
work.summary: Fast Radio Bursts as probes of the circumgalactic and intergalactic media (CGM and IGM).
highlights: Leading spectroscopic observations with Keck and Gemini telescopes
Bayesian inference of matter distribution parameters
Matter density map reconstruction along FRB sightlines

projects.name: The FLIMFLAM Survey
projects.summary: FLIMFLAM is a redshift survey of foreground galaxies along Fast Radio Burst (FRB) sightlines to constrain key parameters describing the distribution of ionized matter in the CGM and IGM to ~20% precision.
highlights: Leading spectroscopic observational efforts with Keck and Gemini telescopes
Matter density map reconstruction and Bayesian inference
Redshift and mass estimation of foreground galaxies

projects.name: Optical Follow-up of Localized FRBs
projects.summary: Current member of the F⁴ team. Involved in planning, execution and data reduction of observations of localized FRBs with optical telescopes.
highlights: Work with CRAFT, MeerTRAP, REALFAST, and DSA collaborations
FRB host galaxy identification and characterization
Study foreground matter along FRB sightlines

projects.name: Keck Visiting Scholar
projects.summary: Characterized the gratings and detector subsystems of the Low-Resolution Imaging Spectrograph (LRIS) on the Keck telescope.
highlights: Produced spectroscopic throughput measurements for three gratings
Automated the monthly checkout procedure for LRIS

projects.name: LRIS Red-side Detector Upgrade
projects.summary: Involved in testing and commissioning of the optical CCD upgrade to LRIS on the Keck telescope.
highlights: Characterized CCD response through measurements of readout noise, gain and linearity

projects.name: Mg II Absorber Clustering
projects.summary: Studied the clustering and distribution of metal absorption lines, specifically the Mg II doublet in quasar spectra.
highlights: Investigated masses of foreground halos contributing to absorption features
